newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW govt confirms CRA-Furukawa deal.
newsitem.headline: NSW govt confirms CRA-Furukawa deal.

text.p: Australia's New South Wales (NSW) state government said on Monday that Japan's Furukawa Co Ltd was involved in a A$250 million investment in RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd's Southern Copper plant.
"The project represents a major economic boost to the region -- with 360 jobs created in the construction phase and 270 jobs once the plant is operational," NSW Premier Bob Carr said in a statement.
"It will also involve an investment of A$250 million," he said. He did not say how much Furukawa would pay for the smelter or if there were any other parties involved.

Earlier the Nihon Keizai Shimbun newspaper in Japan reported that Furukawa Co Ltd and Nissho Iwai Corp have agreed with CRA to buy the Southern Copper smelter and that they would invest over 30 billion yen (A$330 million.)
The plant has not been operating since early 1995 due to tightened pollution regulations.
A spokesman for CRA said he could not comment on such reports. "I can't at this stage confirm that the sale has proceeded," RTZ-CRA spokesman Ian Head told Reuters.
Head declined to comment on the New South Wales government statement or the Nihon Keizai Shimbun report.

Carr said he made the announcement about the re-opening of the Port Kembla copper plant in the southern New South Wales city of Wollongong along with Furukawa Co managing director Akinori Kohra. He said the project would boost wages to the region by A$55 million during the construction phase.
"The smelter will place around 120,000 tonnes of copper per year into the NSW market, replacing about 60,000 tonnes of metal currently imported from interstate or overseas," he said.
The smelter's rehabilitation plan had passed environmental planning tests, he said.
"The improved technology will reduce sulphur dioxide emissions by 89 percent and lead emissions by 92 percent compared to when the plant last operated," he said.
The Japanese firms hope to start operations at the plant in the second half of 1998, the Japanese newspaper said. The plant was capable of producing 80,000 tonnes of copper a year.
